comparison: Python float64 model versus explicitly adapted python_speech_features 0.6 stages
criterion: abs(actual-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference) at every element; exact shapes, indices and finite values required
rationale: Different FFT backends, squared-magnitude evaluation and DCT summation order introduce float64 rounding. A 1e-10 absolute floor protects near-zero coefficients; a 1e-10 relative term also covers large PCM-count-unit power values in the source-check profile. This is much tighter than the proposed float32 C/HW threshold. It is fixed before evaluation, not fitted to evaluation clips.
scope: Python float64 only; not a float32 hardware or fixed-point acceptance budget
development_revision: dev_probe_01 (before any evaluation) preserved failures for source-profile small/full-scale alternating PCM. Raw-count FFT cancellation, zero-only log and lifter produced synthetic MFCC max absolute error about 1.93e-8. Set source-check absolute tolerance to 1e-7; keep comparison_raw13 unchanged. High-magnitude raw power uses the relative term. No input, algorithm or package edits to hide differences.
evaluation_policy: Abort before evaluation if development/synthetic gates fail; bind profiles, tolerance, implementation, verifier, spec and environment hashes in freeze.json. Record native-package policy differences separately from pass/fail comparisons.
